paraphrase: Having taught the Veda, the teacher instructs the pupil: speak the truth; practise dharma; do not neglect your study; having given the teacher the wealth he likes, do not cut off the line of offspring; do not neglect truth, dharma, welfare, prosperity, study and teaching, or the rites to gods and fathers. Let your mother be a god to you, your father, your teacher, your guest. Do only blameless acts, follow only our good conduct. Give with faith, not without faith; give with grace, modesty, awe and understanding. If you are in doubt about an act or conduct, behave as the thoughtful, devoted, gentle brahmins there would behave. This is the rule, the instruction, the secret of the Veda.

paraphrase: In the space within the heart is the person made of mind, immortal and golden. Between the palates hangs something like a nipple: that is the birthplace of Indra (indrayoni), where the hair divides, splitting the skull. Through bhūḥ he enters fire, through bhuvaḥ wind, through suvaḥ the sun, through mahaḥ brahman; he attains self-rule and becomes lord of mind, speech, sight, hearing and understanding — brahman whose body is space, whose self is truth, whose joy is breath, whose bliss is mind, full of peace, immortal.

With the fivefold one wins the fivefold.

paraphrase: The knower of brahman attains the highest. On this there is a verse: brahman is truth, knowledge, infinite (satyaṃ jñānam anantaṃ brahma); whoever knows it hidden in the cave, in the highest heaven, attains all desires together with the wise brahman. From this self space arose, from space wind, from wind fire, from fire water, from water earth, from earth plants, from plants food, from food the person: this person consists of the essence of food.

paraphrase: Different from and within the self made of the essence of food is the self made of breath, which fills it; it too has the shape of a person (head prāṇa, right side vyāna, left side apāna, trunk space, tail earth). Within that is the self made of mind (head the yajus, sides the ṛc and sāman, trunk the teaching, tail the Atharvāṅgiras); within that the self made of understanding (head faith, sides right and truth, trunk yoga, tail greatness); within that the self made of bliss (head joy, sides delight and great delight, trunk bliss, tail — the foundation — brahman). Each inner self is the embodied self of the preceding one.

paraphrase: One who knows brahman as non-being becomes non-being; one who knows 'brahman is', him they know as being. The follow-up questions: does one who does not know go to that world after death, or one who knows? He desired: 'may I become many'; he performed tapas; he created all this; having created it he entered it; having entered it he became the actual and the beyond (sac ca tyac ca), the defined and the undefined, the based and the baseless, understanding and non-understanding, truth and untruth; truth became all this.

paraphrase: In the beginning this was non-being (asat); from it being was born; it made itself by itself; therefore it is called well-made. That which is well-made is the essence (raso vai saḥ); obtaining the essence one becomes blissful; who could breathe, who could live, if this bliss were not in space? When one finds fearless support in that which is invisible, selfless, undefined, without support, one has reached fearlessness; but when one makes the slightest gap in it, there is fear — the fear of one who knows but does not reflect.

paraphrase: From fear of him the wind blows, the sun rises, fire and Indra act, and death runs as the fifth. The inquiry into bliss: let there be a young man, good, learned, quick, firm and strong, and let this whole earth full of wealth be his — that is one human bliss; a hundred human blisses are one bliss of the human gandharvas, and so by hundredfold steps through the divine gandharvas, the fathers of long-lasting world, the gods born so, the gods by works, the gods, Indra, Bṛhaspati and Prajāpati, to one bliss of brahman; and each is also the bliss of a learned man untouched by desire. He who is in the person and he who is in the sun is one; one who knows this, departing, passes into the selves made of food, breath, mind, understanding and bliss.

paraphrase: One who knows the bliss of brahman, from which words turn back with the mind, is never afraid. He is not tormented by the thought 'why did I not do good? why did I do evil?'; knowing thus he frees himself from both.

paraphrase: Bhṛgu Vāruṇi approached his father Varuṇa: 'Sir, teach me brahman.' He named food, breath, sight, hearing, mind and speech, and said: 'That from which these beings are born, by which, once born, they live, and into which they enter on departing — seek to know that; that is brahman.' Bhṛgu performed tapas.

I am food, I am food, I am food! I am the eater of food! I am the maker of verses! I am the first-born of the order (ṛta), before the gods, the navel of immortality. Whoever gives me away has helped me; I, food, eat the eater of food. I have overcome the whole world; my light is like the sun.'

paraphrase: Bhṛgu understood in turn that food is brahman, then breath, then mind, then understanding, each time returning to his father, who said: 'seek to know brahman by tapas; tapas is brahman'. Finally he understood that bliss is brahman, for from bliss beings are born, by bliss they live, into bliss they enter. This knowledge of Bhṛgu, taught by Varuṇa, is established in the highest heaven; whoever knows it becomes established, rich in food, an eater of food, great in offspring, cattle, the lustre of sacred knowledge and fame.

paraphrase: Vows (vrata) concerning food: one should not despise food; one should not reject food; one should make much food; one should turn no one away from one's dwelling, and so should obtain much food and say 'food is ready'. Food and its eater are correlated (breath and body, water and light, earth and space); one should venerate brahman as preservation in speech, as acquisition in breath, as action in the hands, and so on.
